overall_reason: The brand's own Anthropic Sans and Anthropic Serif draw every role, the hero sets its claim in bold sans and runs on in regular serif as one declared signature, and the stylesheet carries tabular-nums, text-wrap and font-synthesis: none.

score.reason: T-TYPE-SOURCE, T-FACE-ROLES, T-LEADING and T-MEASURE pass on the brand's faces with tuned settings; T-HEADLINE-FIT fails on an h1 that runs to 8 lines at 375, and T-PUNCTUATION finds one straight apostrophe beside a curly one.

findings.title: Headlines fit their length
findings.evidence: The h1 holds 201 characters. At 1440 it sets at 40.8px over 3 lines. At 375 it sets at 25px over 8 lines and fills the first screen down to the image. The sweep's h1_words hit (34 words against a maximum of 10) covers the word count; the line count is this lens's.
findings.before: A 201-character statement as the h1, 8 lines at 375
findings.after: Keep the bold sans claim "AI research and products that put safety at the frontier." as the h1 and set the serif run-on as a lead paragraph, or step the serif part down at 375 so the h1 holds to 3 lines
findings.why: At phone width the reader scrolls through eight lines of display type before reaching anything else, and the claim loses its weight against the run-on.

findings.title: Lines break where the sense breaks
findings.evidence: At 375 the three 20px card titles wrap to 2 lines and split the model name: "Introducing Claude / Sonnet 5.5" and "Introducing Claude / Opus 5.5". The type table lists all three as wrapped at 375.
findings.after: A non-breaking space inside "Claude Sonnet 5.5" (or text-wrap: balance on the title) so the model name stays on one line
findings.why: The product name is the point of each card, and the break leaves "Claude" stranded from its model.

findings.title: Punctuation is typeset and consistent
findings.where: Learn more grid, h3.tOQyXa_headline-5 and its summary, 1440 (tiles/1440-02.png)
findings.evidence: The h3 "Claude's Constitution" uses a straight apostrophe, while its summary "A detailed description of our vision for Claude’s values" uses a curly one. The type table counts 1 straight and 1 curly apostrophe on the page.
findings.before: Claude's (straight) in the heading, Claude’s (curly) in the summary
findings.after: A curly apostrophe (’) in the heading to match the rest of the page
findings.why: The two marks sit one line apart in the same card, set in the same face, so the mismatch is visible.

strengths: The brand's own faces: Anthropic Sans for UI, card titles and body, Anthropic Serif for the hero run-on and the carousel titles. fonts.json confirms both drew.
The hero's bold sans claim running into regular serif is one declared signature, used once.
Body leading 1.5, display leading 1.25 with -0.01em tracking; card summaries run a median of 42 characters a line at 1440.
The stylesheet sets tabular-nums, text-wrap: balance and pretty, and font-synthesis: none.
No tracked caps labels in the 1440 layout; dates and categories are sentence case.
not_investigated: T-FIGURES: the only figures are card dates ("Oct 7, 2026") that do not compare in a column.
T-LABEL-TRANSFORM: the two 11px mono carousel counters ("01", "04") at 375 are digits, so their caps transform changes nothing.
Small text at 13 to 15px is the sweep's text_floor finding.
